title: Your Fine-Tuned Model Is Tech Debt: A 50x ROI House of Cards — Dan Bjornn, Lease End
talk_summary: A data scientist describes fine-tuning a small model for customer-intent classification, hitting 50x ROI, then discovering the maintenance cost (week-long retrain cycles, regressions, model/architecture lock-in) made it tech debt. They rebuilt as a model-agnostic agentic system where fixes are prompt/skill/context edits deployed as MD files, cutting fix time from a week to under an hour with better accuracy at slightly higher per-message cost but lower total cost.

takeaways.technique: Skills/context files over retraining for behavior fixes
takeaways.what_they_do: Behavior lives in editable skill/prompt/context files (MD uploaded to S3) rather than model weights, so a defect fix is a text edit plus validation, not a retrain pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you adjust the simp system prompt or the skill that was affected, we validated performance on a curated set
takeaways.numbers: fix cycle reduced from ~1 week to <1 hour

takeaways.technique: Curated regression set accumulated from production
takeaways.what_they_do: They collected a curated evaluation set from real production traffic over time and validated every prompt/skill change against it before deploy, catching regressions the fix would otherwise cause.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we validated performance on a curated set that we had been collecting over the time that this was in production

takeaways.technique: Model-agnostic agent framework, swap models freely
takeaways.what_they_do: They built the agentic framework model-agnostic so any provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, others) can be used, with the value concentrated in context rather than a specific model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our agentic framework was built model agnostic, so we could use OpenAI, we can use uh Anthropic

takeaways.technique: Optimize total cost, not per-message cost
takeaways.what_they_do: They accepted higher per-message API cost for better models because total cost fell once maintenance/retraining labor was counted.
takeaways.evidence_quote: while it cost us a little more per message, the total cost went down because we were spending far less time trying to keep it up and running
takeaways.numbers: higher per-message cost, lower total cost

takeaways.what_they_do: Before any costly retrain they asked: how frequent is the issue, is it hurting the customer badly, and can a cheap band-aid prevent the expensive cycle.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Is there anything that we can do in order to prevent a retrain? Can we have some kind of a band-aid fix

takeaways.what_they_do: They found that dropping in better context/resources improved results more than changing models, mirroring how Claude Code worked without model changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You drop in the better better context, you get better results.
